messages:
kevin: Heads up — after the route-label rename the console eviction metrics show a big chunk of nulls for route-based aggregations. Dashboards that group by route are missing traffic.

marta: Is this definitely a schema change or an ingest mapping bug? I looked at raw events and some have `route_v2` & some have `route` still.

omar: We started shipping `route_v2` from the frontend last Thursday. Ingest pipeline hasn't normalized it into our analytics envelope. So it's partly mapping, partly storage model mismatch.

elyse: UI rollout is at ~10% behind a feature flag. We expected telemetry to be compatible but sounds like the new field wasn't plumbed through. Need it stable for canary -> 100% rollout.

kevin: Proposal draft: add two nullable columns to console_events: `route_alias` (text) and `eviction_reason` (text/enum). At ingest we write both the legacy `route` and new `route_v2` into `route_alias` (coalesced), and write explicit `eviction_reason` when eviction occurs. Keep read queries using `coalesce(route_alias, route)` so existing dashboards keep working. Backfill historic events into `route_alias` for the last 90 days via streaming job.

omar: SQL snippet for starters (Postgres):
```sql
ALTER TABLE console_events
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS route_alias TEXT,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS eviction_reason TEXT;
-- create index concurrently to avoid locks
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_console_events_route_alias ON console_events(route_alias);
```
Note: if table is partitioned we'll need to touch partitions or use BRIN if ranges make sense.

marta: Backfill/windowing question — running a 90-day backfill on the full table will be expensive. Any chance we can do incremental windows (24h) and cap worker concurrency? Need rough cost estimate before budget signoff.

sam: We can do the backfill via CDC -> kafka -> Spark job that writes parquet to temp table then upserts in batches. That keeps write pressure low and is resumable. Or use Debezium stream to re-emit events and let existing ingest adapters handle normalization.

elyse: Also need to update dashboards/Looker explores: add `route_alias` to the explore and change default filter logic to `coalesce(route_alias, route)`. I can own the dashboard changes but need mapping docs for the analytics team.

kevin: Suggested rollout plan:
1) Schema change: add columns + indexes (CONCURRENTLY)
2) Ingest adapter change: dual-write `route_alias` and set `eviction_reason` where applicable (deploy in canary)
3) Run incremental backfill for last 90 days (24h windows) with low concurrency; monitor write QPS and table bloat
4) Update dashboard queries and saved explores to use `coalesce(route_alias, route)`
5) Monitor for 30d; after 180d remove legacy read paths and maybe drop `route` if it's safe

omar: Indexing detail — for heavily partitioned storage we should prefer per-partition indexes created concurrently. For Postgres main table we should avoid any non-concurrent DDL. Also consider a BRIN index if route cardinality is high and queries are mostly time-bounded.

marta: Cost ballpark from infra: ~2k compute hours for the backfill job at low concurrency, ~6k USD. Also small I/O and index maintenance ops. If that's correct, finance OKs with an owner.

kevin: I'll open the infra budget PR and schedule a canary run for one tenant. Canary timeline: after ingest adapter deployed to canary (feature flag) we'll run a 48h incremental backfill limited to that tenant, validate dashboards, then expand.

sam: For safety, emit a `telemetry_migration.v1` event at ingest for every normalized write. That gives us an easy audit trail and lets regressions be queried.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: canary backfill job starting at 1755555590 — job id bkf-2024-07-xx-01

elyse: I'll coordinate dashboard updates and publish a short migration guide for product/ops teams about the coalesce behavior and timeline.

kevin: If no strong objections by EOD I'll file the formal migration RFC/Runbook and create the PRs for DDL + ingest adapter. Thx all. :thumbsup:
